Shell.SettingsDescription: Set your defaults once. Connect a cloud account whenever you're ready.
Shell.DifferentOutput: You can choose a different destination each time you preserve recordings.
Shell.DefaultFormat: Default file type for easy-to-play files
Shell.GuideNext: Guide me to the next step
Shell.GuideDescription: The app moves from Connect to Discover by itself when a recorder connects, and from Preserve to Archive when your recordings are saved.
Shell.GuideManual: You can always move between steps yourself using the journey navigation.
Shell.CacheDescription: Recordings downloaded for a preview or for their details, and the short preview clips, are stored here. Saving a recording does not use this folder. They are removed when you close the application, or at once with the button below. A changed folder is used from the next start of the application.
Shell.ClearCacheHelp: This removes the downloads and preview clips made for previews in this session. Saved recordings are kept.
Shell.ToolsDescription: MediaInfoLib is part of the application. FFmpeg and FFprobe are not part of it: the installer downloads them if you leave that option ticked, and you can download them here at any time. Fill in a location below only to use your own copy.
Shell.Ffmpeg.InUsePinned: FFmpeg in use: {0} · version {1}, checked against the recorded checksum
Shell.Ffmpeg.InUseOther: FFmpeg in use: {0}. This is not FFmpeg {1}, the build this version of the application is made for. Download it below; the application then uses the downloaded copy.
Shell.Ffmpeg.InUseOnPath: FFmpeg in use: {0} (found on PATH; the application does not check which version it is). You can download FFmpeg {1} below; the application then uses that copy.
Shell.Ffmpeg.Missing: FFmpeg is not installed. It is needed to save a recording as an easy-to-play file (MKV, MP4 or MPEG) and for the preview. Exact copies, recording details and cloud upload work without it.
Shell.Ffmpeg.DownloadHelp: Downloads the FFmpeg {0} “essentials” build of its distributor, Gyan Doshi, from his GitHub releases (github.com/GyanD/codexffmpeg), or from gyan.dev if that fails. The download is checked against the SHA-256 recorded in this application, and ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe are kept in {1}. FFmpeg is licensed under the GNU GPL version 3; its licence text is saved beside it.
Shell.Ffmpeg.InstalledHelp: FFmpeg {0} was downloaded, verified and saved. Easy-to-play files and the preview are available now.
Shell.Ffmpeg.NoticeHelp: An easy-to-play file (MKV, MP4 or MPEG) and the preview need FFmpeg. An exact copy works without it.
Shell.Ffmpeg.UpdateHelp: The FFmpeg on this PC is not version {0}, the one this version of the application is made for. Download it to get its fixes.
Shell.Ffmpeg.RequiredForContainer: An easy-to-play file needs FFmpeg, which is not installed. Download it with the button on this page, or choose “Exact copy”.
Shell.Ffmpeg.RequiredForPreview: The preview needs FFmpeg, which is not installed. Download it with the button on this page. “Download and show details” works without it.
Shell.Ffmpeg.RequiredForCheck: FFmpeg is not installed, so there is nothing to check yet. Download it first, or enter the location of your own copy.
Shell.CloudDescription: Optional. You sign in through your browser, and nothing is uploaded until you choose to upload on the Archive page.
Shell.UploadToAccessible: Cloud destination for uploads and for the cloud view
Shell.UploadToHelp: Files from the Archive page are uploaded to this destination, and the Cloud page shows what it holds. You can change it at any time; the choice is remembered.
Shell.NotConnected: Not connected. Choose Connect OneDrive and sign in with your Microsoft account; nothing else is needed.
Shell.GoogleNotConnected: Not connected. Google Drive needs a one-time setup at Google first.
Shell.SignInEnded: The sign-in has ended. Connect again; the rest stays as it is.
Shell.MicrosoftConsent: Microsoft will ask whether this application may have full access to your files; when a folder for uploads is set below, it asks about all files you can access, because that folder may belong to someone else. The application uses the permission only to add new files to the top folder of your OneDrive, or to the folder set below, and to list that folder; it never changes or deletes a file that is already there.
Shell.GoogleSecretHelp: The secret is kept with the saved sign-in, protected for your Windows account, and never written to the settings file. A secret you typed is remembered until you close the application; it is saved once you have connected.
Shell.GoogleSecretSaved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it
Shell.GoogleSevenDays: While your Google project is in the status Testing, Google ends the sign-in seven days after you connect, and you connect again; the client ID and secret stay as they are. The guide explains how to remove that limit.
Shell.GoogleClientShape: A Google client ID ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com. Paste the Client ID of your Desktop app client; the client secret goes into the field below it.
Shell.BuiltInPlaceholder: Empty: the built-in ID is used
Shell.BuiltInClient: Leave the field empty to use the application ID built into the application ({0}). It identifies the application to Microsoft and is not a password.
Shell.MicrosoftSetupDescription: Most people do not need this. It is for those who prefer their own registration, or whose organisation blocks the built-in one. The guide below explains the registration step by step; paste its Application (client) ID here.
Shell.MicrosoftPermissions: The registration needs the delegated permissions Files.ReadWrite and offline_access and no client secret. Add Files.ReadWrite.All as well if uploads go to a shared folder.
Shell.MicrosoftClientShape: A Microsoft application ID has the form 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000. Paste the Application (client) ID of your registration, or clear the field to use the built-in one.
Shell.SwitchAccount: To use another account, choose Connect again: the sign-in page lets you pick the account. There is no need to disconnect first.
Shell.OneDriveFolderPlaceholder: Link to a shared folder; empty means the top folder
Shell.OneDriveFolderHelp: With the link to a shared OneDrive or SharePoint folder, uploads go into that folder instead of the top folder of your OneDrive, the Cloud page shows it, and the link beside an uploaded file opens it for everyone the folder is shared with, whichever account their browser is signed in to. The account connected here must be allowed to add files to the folder. Connect OneDrive after setting the folder: Microsoft is then asked for the permission that a folder belonging to someone else needs. The link is kept on this PC, encrypted for your Windows account.
Shell.OneDriveFolderGuide: How to share a folder and use its link ↗
Shell.OneDriveFolderCheckedHelp: Uploads to OneDrive now go to the folder “{0}”. Whether the connected account may add files there shows with the first upload.
Shell.OneDriveFolderOwnFiles: The sign-in on this PC reaches only the connected account's own files. That is enough when the folder is that account's own; if it belongs to someone else, connect OneDrive again and Microsoft will ask for the permission a shared folder needs.
Shell.OneDriveFolderConnectFirst: The link is saved. Connect OneDrive to check it: the folder is looked up with the connected account.
Shell.OneDriveFolderEmpty: No folder is set, so uploads go to the top folder of your OneDrive. Paste the link to a shared folder to change that.
Shell.DisconnectGoogle.Title: Disconnect Google Drive?
Shell.DisconnectGoogle.Message:
This removes the saved sign-in from this PC, and with it the saved client secret. To connect again you will need the secret, which Google does not show a second time.

The application also asks Google to end the sign-in. That ends it on every PC that uses the same Google client with this account.

To use another Google account you do not have to disconnect: choose Connect Google Drive and pick the account.
Shell.GoogleSetupTitle: What Google Drive may do, and the seven-day limit
Shell.GoogleSetupDescription: Google does not allow an open-source application to bring its own Google credentials, so you create a small Google Cloud project once (about 15 minutes, free): 1. create a project and enable the Google Drive API; 2. describe the sign-in screen and add your own Google address as a test user; 3. create an OAuth client of the type Desktop app; 4. paste its client ID and client secret below. Google shows the secret only once.
Shell.GooglePermissions: The application asks Google only for access to the files it creates itself. It cannot see or change anything else in your Drive.
Shell.CloudSaveHelp: Connecting and disconnecting also save the settings on this page. A sign-in belongs to the application or client ID it was made with: after changing the ID you connect again. Disconnect removes every sign-in saved on this PC for that service; for Google Drive the application also asks Google to end the sign-in. The permission you gave at Microsoft stays until you remove it on your account's page; the setup guide says where.
Shell.UnsavedChanges: This page holds changes that are not saved yet. Choose Save preferences at the bottom of the window to keep them.
Shell.PreferencesSavedHelp: Your defaults are ready for this session and the next time you open AMG DIGA Archive.
Shell.AboutDescription: A native Windows application for saving recordings from a network recorder over DLNA and keeping a copy in the cloud, built with WinUI 3, FFmpeg and MediaInfoLib.
Shell.ProjectLink: AMG DIGA Archive · project and releases ↗
Shell.ReleasesLink: Look for a newer version on the releases page ↗
Shell.ReleasesHelp: The application never looks for updates by itself. This copy contains .NET {0}, Windows App SDK {1} and MediaInfoLib {2}; only a new version of the application updates them.
Shell.LogHelp: When something goes wrong, its technical details are written to an error log on this PC: {0}. It can name folders, recording titles and the recorder's address. It holds no passwords and no sign-ins, is kept small, and never leaves this PC unless you send it to someone yourself.

Shell.NeedGoogleSecret: Enter your Google client secret before connecting. Google shows it only when the client is created; if it is lost, add a new secret to the client in Google Cloud.
Shell.AccountDisconnectedHelp: The saved sign-in was removed from this PC. The permission you gave at Microsoft stays until you remove it on your account's page.
Shell.AccountDisconnectedEnded: The saved sign-in was removed from this PC, and Google confirmed that the sign-in has ended.
Shell.AccountDisconnectedNotEnded: The saved sign-in was removed from this PC. Google did not confirm that the sign-in has ended; you can remove the permission on your Google account's page.

Shell.LanguageHelp: “Use Windows language” takes the first supported language from your Windows language preferences. If none is supported, English is used. Number and date formats still follow your Windows regional settings.

Shell.LanguagePending: A saved language change will apply when you next open the app.
